rationale:
I judge the tests adequate for `requirements.sdk.outlines.selection`. I did not request implementation source, because the supplied tests were enough to map each obligation.

**Resolution from the root and the owned result**
- `unicode_spans_use_bytes_and_whitespace_only_lines_create_no_items` selects each line item by its selector and checks the text.
- `rust_items_attach_documentation_and_preserve_structural_hashes` selects every outline item, including the root `""`. For each it asserts that the selected text equals the source slice and that the structural hash matches the item's. It also selects `mod[auth]/fn[check]` and checks that the text includes the attached doc comment and attribute, which covers `text()` returning the attached source.
- `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits` checks `id()` on selected content (`selected.id() == &id`).
- `formatted_contents_redact_credentials_while_retaining_raw_text_and_spans` checks that `text()` returns the original text before redaction, while `format()` redacts it.

**Sharing the snapshot and fingerprinting rules**
- `std::ptr::eq(second.outline(), contents.outline())` in the markdown test, and the same check in the Rust test, show that the outline is shared with the original handle.
- `explicit_languages_share_configuration_and_retain_their_scheme` selects `part[selected]` from content built with an explicit language. It asserts that the selected fingerprint is the same whether the file was loaded from a path or supplied as source. It also asserts that the language, the fingerprint scheme and the structural hash are retained, and that a different scheme (`custom-v3`) gives a different fingerprint.

**No additional file read and use after the handle is dropped**
- In `selected_contents_outlive_handles_and_later_file_edits`, the original `file` is dropped and the file on disk is rewritten.
- `selected_again` (selected before the drop) still returns `"second"`.
- `selected.select("")` after the drop and the edit returns the original root text `"first\nsecond\n"`. A fresh `from_id` fails, so the retained snapshot was used rather than a re-read of the file.

**Selector syntax applied during selection**
- Percent-encoded names and `#N` duplicates are resolved in `markdown_heading_levels_resolve_encoded_duplicates_and_anonymous_items`.
- Anonymous `section@` and `block@` selectors are resolved in the same markdown test.
- `css_duplicate_names_are_numbered_after_normalization_within_each_parent` selects `rule[a%20b]#1` and `#2`, and `media[print]#2/rule[a]`. It also checks that the un-numbered `rule[a%20b]` is an error.
- The empty selector selecting the root is checked in several tests.
- Identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. `unknown_extensions_keep_nonblank_lines_and_content_selectors` checks that equal lines share a selector and that selecting it works. `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` selects a duplicated line selector from `"same\nsame"` and gets the text.

**Errors**
- `missing_file_and_invalid_selections_are_errors` checks a malformed selector (`fn[`) and a missing item (`fn[absent]`).
- `ambiguous_items_are_errors_except_for_identical_plain_text_lines` checks that duplicate non-`line` items give an "ambiguous" error. It also checks that `line` items with differing hashes give the same error.
- The CSS test's un-numbered duplicate selection is a further ambiguity error.

I found no unpinned obligation or boundary the text names. Every `{test}` reference to the subject is present on the relevant tests, so there is no marking gap.

text: :::{req} selection
`OutlineContent::select` resolves a selector from the file's root against the
retained outline. It returns another owned `OutlineContent` for that item,
sharing the original source snapshot and fingerprinting rules. Selection
performs no additional file read and remains usable after the original handle
is dropped. Resolution follows
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax`, including its rule that
identical plain-text lines are interchangeable. Invalid, missing, or ambiguous
selections return an error under {cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.errors`.
```rust,ignore
impl OutlineContent {
/// Select an item from this retained file snapshot.
pub fn select(&self, selector: &str) -> Result<Self, OutlineError>;
/// Address of the selected item.
pub fn id(&self) -> &OutlineData;
/// Original selected text, including attached source, before redaction.
pub fn text(&self) -> &str;
:::{req} selector_syntax
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} errors
The outline API makes a best effort to recover from parse errors.
File-read and unrecoverable parsing failures return errors, distinct from
successful contents for an empty file. Selecting a language commits to that
language's parsing rules.
A malformed selector, a missing item, or an ambiguity not permitted by
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.selector_syntax` also returns an error.
